hero.title: Yale's student chapter for assistive design
hero.text: Formerly Yale e-NABLE and now a TOM chapter, Y-AID is a student-led coalition of engineers and medical students creating open-source assistive technology.
hero.imageAlt: Two students adjusting a large 3D printer frame

mission.title: Healthcare built with the community
paragraphs: Yale Assistive Innovation and Design, formerly Yale e-NABLE and a current TOM chapter, seeks to contribute to the Greater New Haven community by providing free, customizable assistive devices to those in need.
Using both TOM-based and original designs, Y-AID plays a unique role in providing much-needed healthcare in collaboration with engineers, clinicians and community members.
mission.imageAlt: Three students in masks and gloves casting silicone parts in the lab

history.title: From Yale e-NABLE to Y-AID
history.text: Six years of building, from one printed hand to eight projects with hospitals and clinics.

events.title: An official e-NABLE chapter
events.text: Yale e-NABLE joined the international e-NABLE network in January after printing its first prototype hand under founder Grayson Wagner, BS ’23.

events.title: The cello arm
events.text: In November the club made the cover of Yale Engineering magazine with a prosthetic designed for an 11-year-old so she could play the cello.

events.title: Davis and Williams projects
events.text: The club built up two long-term projects: the Davis project, an active arm support, and the Williams project, a pediatric arm prosthetic.

events.title: A cello app and a wheelchair scale
events.text: The team added a mobile app to the cello project, continued the Davis and Williams builds, and started the wheelchair scale.

events.title: Y-AID and TOM
events.text: The club became Yale Assistive Innovation and Design and joined the global network of TOM chapters, taking on larger projects and buildathons.

events.title: New clinical partners
events.text: Expanding through Bridgeport Hospital, the Yale School of Medicine and the University of New Haven’s Tagliatela College of Engineering.

affiliations.title: The organizations behind our work
affiliations.text: Funding, space, clinical referrals and medical guidance all come from these partners.
